title: Security review: Encryption & KMS/BYOK/HSM - QuantumBank
summary: High-level review of encryption at-rest and in-transit, customer-managed key options (BYOK), HSM constraints, audit logging, key rotation, and performance tradeoffs. Agreed next steps to exchange SOC2/pen test artifacts, provide BYOK architecture diagram, and run a small benchmark to measure latency impact of envelope encryption + HSM signing.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-24 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Ivy (Redwood SE), Ava (CISO, QuantumBank), Liam (Head of Infra), Sophie (Security Engineer), Noah (Compliance)

Summary (auto): quick run through of encryption options, BYOK questions, HSM exportability and attestation, perf impact, and next steps to validate with artifacts and a benchmark.

00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. Quick roll call?
00:06 - Ava: Hi, Ava here, CISO at QuantumBank.
00:08 - Liam: Liam, head of infra.
00:10 - Sophie: Sophie, security eng.
00:12 - Noah: Noah, compliance.
00:14 - Daniel: Daniel from Redwood, SE on infra and security.
00:17 - Maya: Awesome. Today we want to focus on encryption at rest and in transit, our KMS options, BYOK, and HSM questions you raised in the intake.
00:25 - Ava: Yes, key questions: can keys be customer-managed, do you support HSM-backed keys, can we rotate without downtime, and what audit logs are available, also any perf hit?
00:35 - Daniel: Great, we can go through flow. At a high level Redwood supports envelope encryption - we store encrypted data keys (DEKs) and use a customer-managed key (CMK) in your KMS to wrap/unwrap the DEK. That means the actual model artifacts and cached KV are encrypted at rest with the DEK and only the KMS sees the KEK operations.
00:49 - Sophie: So DEK/KEK, yeah okay. Does Redwood ever hold the unencrypted DEK or is it strictly sealed?
00:57 - Daniel: We never persist plaintext DEKs on disk. The runtime keeps the DEK in memory for the short-lived session, and we require TLS in transit. If you choose BYOK we integrate your CMK for wrap/unwrap calls.
01:10 - Liam: What about HSM? We use an HSM vendor internally (Thales) and they require that keys never leave the HSM and signing happens in the HSM. Does Redwood support HSM-backed CMKs in AWS KMS or external HSMs?
01:24 - Ivy: We support AWS KMS with HSM-backed keys (i.e. AWS KMS custom key material or KMS keys with AWS-hosted HSMs). For external, you can use CloudHSM or an HSM backed KMS like VaultCorp, but that requires some additional network/VPC routing for the calls and a validated connectivity pattern for Private deployments.
01:40 - Ava: If we use BYOK with an external HSM, can Redwood call the HSM directly or do we need to proxy through our KMS?
01:49 - Daniel: Typically Redwood calls your managed KMS endpoint (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). That KMS is responsible for talking to the HSM. If you have an external HSM outside public cloud, the recommended approach is to deploy Redwood Private in your VPC/on-prem and allow Redwood to access the KMS endpoint over private networking. We don't host keys in our control plane for BYOK—Redwood's control plane stores only key references and metadata, not key material.
02:12 - Sophie: Do you support import of key material into AWS KMS (ImportKeyMaterial flow)? We currently generate keys in our HSM and import to KMS for cross-account usage.
02:21 - Daniel: We do not perform import on your behalf, but we support the pattern. You can import key material into your KMS and then provide Redwood the ARN to use. We will make KMS Encrypt/Decrypt calls.
02:30 - Noah: For auditability, we need key usage logs showing which services/callers requested decrypts and when. Do you surface those in Redwood Console and can they be exported to our SIEM?
02:41 - Maya: Yes, we provide detailed audit logs at token/key-call level. They can be streamed to your cloud logging (CloudWatch/Logging/Stackdriver) or exported to a Syslog/SIEM. Logs include caller identity, resource ARN, timestamp, and request id. We also keep internal traces per request ID to map model inference to a key operation, subject to retention policies.
03:02 - Liam: Retention policies — what are default retention windows and can we extend for regulatory needs?
03:08 - Ivy: Default audit retention is 90 days in the hosted plan; for enterprise / dedicated you can configure longer retention or ship logs out to your storage for indefinite retention. For Private deployments you fully control retention.
03:20 - Ava: Compliance wise, we need FIPS 140-2 level HSM attestations and SOC 2. Do you have those?
03:28 - Maya: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and we can share the report under NDA. For FIPS/HSM we rely on the KMS/HSM vendor compliance, e.g., AWS KMS with FIPS endpoints or HSMs from Thales/Entrust provides attestation. We maintain documentation mapping our controls to SOC2/ISO requirements.
03:45 - Sophie: Ok, practical question: what is the perf penalty for calling KMS on every inference? Our workloads are sensitive to a few ms of added latency.
03:55 - Daniel: Good point. We use envelope encryption and DEK caching with tight TTLs. The common pattern is to unwrap the DEK once per secured session or per container start and then cache it in memory; subsequent inferences use the DEK locally. That means KMS calls are relatively infrequent. For HSM-backed CMKs there's an additional signing/verifying step for key attestation sometimes, but typical added latency per inference is negligible when DEKs are cached. If you need sub-50ms tail latency we can tune TTLs and run benchmarks.
04:22 - Liam: How about multi-tenant isolation — if we use hosted Redwood can you guarantee that data is logically segregated and keys are isolated per customer?
04:32 - Daniel: Yes hosted multi-tenant ensures encryption separation: each customer gets their own DEK namespace and key references. With BYOK the CMK is in your account and the wrapping/unwrapping operations are under your control. For strict isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private.
04:45 - Ava: For incident response we need key rotation procedures with no downtime and ability to revoke keys quickly. How is rotation handled?
04:53 - Ivy: Rotation is handled by creating a new CMK version and re-wrapping DEKs. We support asynchronous rewrap where we continue to accept the old DEK until all objects are rotated. We can also do immediate cutover if you prefer. Revocation: you can disable the CMK in KMS, and Redwood will fail-wrapping/unwrapping accordingly; we have documented runbooks for key revocation and emergency procedures.
05:18 - Noah: Do you keep copies of archived DEKs or key material in backups?
05:22 - Daniel: No plaintext key material is stored in backups. Encrypted DEKs are stored, and backups of encrypted blobs are kept; but key material is never included.
05:30 - Sophie: About in-transit encryption, do you support mTLS between Redwood runtime and our VPC endpoints?
05:36 - Ivy: Yes, for Private deployments we support mTLS and mutual auth. For hosted we require TLS1.2/1.3; if you need mTLS we recommend Private.
05:45 - Liam: Any limitations with HSM-backed keys for large batch workloads? For example, if every job requires a KMS sign call it could balloon costs and latency.
05:55 - Daniel: Right, that's why we avoid per-token KMS calls. For batch jobs we unwrap once, or use a per-job DEK. If your policy requires an HSM sign per job we can design batching to amortize calls. We can also cache ephemeral DEKs per worker. Cost-wise KMS calls add per-request charge so we'll factor that into cost estimates.
06:18 - Ava: We use strict key rotation every 90 days and require key attestation after rotation. Any tool support for automating this?
06:26 - Maya: We provide automation scripts and can integrate with your KMS key policies to enforce rotation. Daniel can share a rotation playbook.
06:32 - Sophie: Certificate management for clients and services, do you integrate with our internal PKI?
06:37 - Daniel: Yes, for Private we can integrate with your PKI for mTLS certs. For hosted, certificates are Redwood-managed but we can support SAML SSO and RBAC mapping to teams.
06:46 - Ava: Regarding audit logs, can you tie model predictions to key usage for a forensics trail? We need to show which model response used which key and who invoked it.
06:55 - Ivy: We correlate request IDs across tracing and key usage logs. When a decrypt call occurs we log the request id and correlation id to allow forensic chaining: request -> model inference -> key unwrap. This is included in the enterprise audit exports.
07:08 - Liam: Data residency: we need the data and key operations to stay in EU for some products. Does Redwood support region locking for KMS calls and storage?
07:17 - Daniel: Yes region pinning is supported. For hosted you can choose a region and KMS endpoint in that region. For stricter requirements Dedicated and Private give you full control. If you need cross-region replication we can handle that with explicit consent and controls.
07:29 - Sophie: A question about backup keys — if a container migrates to another host does the DEK move in memory? Is there a risk of leaking DEK in logs?
07:36 - Daniel: DEKs are in-memory only and we do not log plaintext DEKs. Telemetry logs contain key references only. If a container is migrated we rely on secure memory wipe and re-initialize DEKs via KMS unwrap during startup.
07:50 - Ava: For third-party audits, will you allow KMS call logs and role mappings to be shared with our auditors?
07:57 - Maya: Under NDA we can provide logs or facilitate auditor access; there are standard procedures for Customer audit access. For hosted customers we provide redacted logs as needed.
08:06 - Noah: Incident response tabletop: if a KMS key is compromised how fast can we rotate and what is rollback plan?
08:14 - Ivy: We have runbooks: disable CMK, revoke access policies, rotate DEKs by re-wrapping with new CMK, update runtime to use new key. For critical keys we can execute emergency rotation within the hour subject to coordination. We will share the runbook.
08:26 - Liam: Any constraints on HSM attestation frequency or remote attestations? Our compliance requires quarterly attestation of HSM key material.
08:34 - Daniel: Attestation is handled by the HSM vendor/KMS; Redwood consumes those attestations as part of compliance artifacts. We can include attestation metadata in our audit package.
08:44 - Sophie: About key deletion: GDPR/Right to be forgotten — we need to ensure we can delete customer data and associated keys. How is deletion handled?
08:52 - Daniel: Deletion of keys in KMS has standard safeguards; we recommend disabling keys then scheduling deletion per your retention policy. For data deletion we will zero out or remove encrypted blobs and purge backups as requested. Private deployments fully control deletion lifecycle.
09:07 - Ava: Any gotchas with BYOK per your prior customers?
09:11 - Maya: Common gotchas: 1) Not planning for KMS request volume causing throttling — we recommend testing; 2) Misconfiguring IAM roles for cross-account calls; 3) Assuming no perf impact without validating DEK TTLs. We'll help with checklists.
09:27 - Liam: For our pilot we want to try a hosted flow with BYOK using AWS KMS (HSM backed) and measure latency. What do you need from us?
09:36 - Ivy: Ideally an IAM role with Encrypt/Decrypt permissions and a test CMK ARN, plus sample request patterns and target latency/throughput. We'll run a small benchmark in a safe staging environment.
09:48 - Sophie: Also need to confirm how Redwood stores key ARNs in the control plane and what metadata is visible to support teams.
09:56 - Daniel: We store the key ARN and metadata (region, key id) and store nothing sensitive about key material. Support can see key ARNs for diagnostics but access to call KMS is gated and requires customer authorization for BYOK scenarios.
10:10 - Maya: Quick recap of next steps: we'll share SOC2 and pen test, Daniel will send the BYOK architecture diagram and rotation playbook, and we'll schedule a perf session. Anything else?
10:19 - Ava: We'd like to see an example runbook for emergency key rotation.
10:22 - Maya: Daniel will add that to the docs.
10:24 - Noah: Also please include log format examples for the SIEM ingestion.
10:29 - Ivy: We'll include sample CloudWatch/Stackdriver export snippets.
10:33 - Liam: When can we run the perf session? 2026-07-07 as mentioned works.
10:36 - Ivy: I'll send the calendar invite.
10:40 - Sophie: One last question — does Redwood support HSM-backed signing for attestation of inference outputs? We want cryptographic proof that outputs were produced by a key inside HSM at a given time.
10:52 - Daniel: We can support HSM signing as an additional step; that would be an HSM-generated signature over a request id or hash of the output. It adds some latency for the signing step but can be batched. We'll include a design note.
10:59 - Maya: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and the invite.
11:03 - Ava: Thanks, bye.
11:04 - Meeting end.

Notes: transcript contains some auto-stt artifacts, names/terms occasionally mangled. Action items recorded above.
